findings.affected_surface: CLI option parsing for slapadd tool's -o option
findings.old_behavior: The slapadd tool's -o option parser did not recognize 'remove-sids'. An unrecognized option would cause parse_slapopt() to return -1 immediately after falling through the existing option branch chain.
findings.new_behavior: The slapadd tool's -o option parser now recognizes 'remove-sids=<sid>[,<sid>,...]'. When used, it parses the comma-separated SID values, validates each SID (0..SLAP_SYNC_SID_MAX), stores them in sids_to_remove[], sets update_ctxcsn=1, and implies -w (overwrite sync context). If the same sid is configured as the serverID via -S, slapadd exits with error. If a SID value is out of range, it prints an error and returns -1. Other tools (slapcat, slapindex, slapdn) receive a debug message 'remove-sids meaningless for tool.' and continue.
findings.compatibility_reason: This is an additive, opt-in CLI option change. All existing behavior is preserved when the option is not used because sids_to_remove is zero-initialized (BSS), making all new conditional branches inactive. No existing slapadd script or invocation will break. The option is additive only and does not modify any existing CLI behavior or defaults. The internal tool_vars struct change in slapcommon.h is an implementation detail not exposed to consumers.
findings.why_not_internal_only: The change modifies CLI option parsing in parse_slapopt(), which is the central option dispatcher for all slap tools. Adding a new recognized option key to the -o option namespace is a user-visible CLI surface change. Additionally, the entryCSN replacement and contextCSN filtering logic in slapadd's entry_free() and slap_tool_update_ctxcsn() alters the persistent database state when the option is used, which is observable by downstream LDAP consumers (replicated databases receive CSNs with the local SID instead of the original). However, for users not using the new option, all behavior is identical.
findings.uncertainty: No uncertainty — the patch is a straightforward additive feature. All new code paths are guarded by sids_to_remove[] being non-zero, which only occurs when the user explicitly passes the new option.
findings.recommended_review: No breaking changes expected. Verify that slapadd operates identically to the baseline when -o remove-sids= is not used.
findings.test_recommendation: 1) Verify slapadd runs without the new option and produces identical output to baseline. 2) Verify the new option correctly parses SID values and rejects invalid ones. 3) Verify that CSNs for removed SIDs are replaced with local CSNs. 4) Verify contextCSN excludes removed SIDs.
